req.title: Redirect count boundary
req.statement: The system shall accept /redirect/<n> with n in the range 1..30 inclusive and reject values above.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states /redirect/<n> accepts n in [1..30] inclusive and rejects values above 30. Key boundaries are: n=1 (lower bound), n=30 (upper bound), n=31 (first rejected value above upper bound). We also need a mid-range positive case (EP), a zero/negative case (NEG for assert n>0), and exact status code assertions. The source code shows: assert n > 0 (so n=0 triggers AssertionError/500), and the redirect chain eventually resolves to /get. For n>30, httpbin returns 404 (Flask route constraint not matched for large ints, or the app returns 404). Actually reviewing the source: there is no explicit upper-bound check in redirect_n_times — the route accepts any int. However the requirement says reject above 30. We must test what the SUT actually does. The source shows no upper-bound guard, so n=31 may return a redirect chain. We test the stated requirement boundaries precisely: n=1 (BVA lower), n=30 (BVA upper), n=31 (NEG/BVA above upper), n=15 (EP mid-range), n=0 (NEG, triggers assert). For n=0 the Flask test client will get a 500 (AssertionError). For n=31 the requirement says reject (4xx), but the source has no guard — we assert what the requirement mandates. This makes the tests requirement-traceable and mutation-resilient by asserting exact status codes.

from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_positive():
    r = client.get('/redirect/1', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    data = r.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'url' in data

test_redirect_n1_lower_boundary_positive()

tests.name: test_redirect_n2_chain_resolves_positive
preconditions: n=2 exercises the relative redirect branch
actions: GET /redirect/2 without following redirects to check first hop
GET /redirect/2 with follow_redirects=True to check final resolution
expected: First hop: HTTP 302 with Location containing /redirect/1
trace: R-HTTPBIN-048: n=2 is valid; source: _redirect('relative', n, False) for n>1 non-absolute
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_n2_chain_resolves_positive():
    r_hop = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r_hop.status_code == 302
    location = r_hop.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert '/redirect/1' in location, f'Expected /redirect/1 in Location, got: {location}'
    r_final = client.get('/redirect/2', follow_redirects=True)
    assert r_final.status_code == 200
    data = r_final.get_json()
    assert data is not None
    assert 'url' in data

test_redirect_n2_chain_resolves_positive()
